summary: How the Roman Republic's elite, by murdering the Gracchi in 133 BCE, opened a century of street-gang politics and civil war that ended with Augustus creating Rome's militarized police, secret police and the Praetorian Guard.

evidence.note: Last king Tarquin and the Lucretia story leading to the revolt
Republic founded 509 BCE after the last king is expelled
Public land absorbed by rich estates worked by slaves, veterans dispossessed
Tiberius Gracchus introduced; his land reform drives the rest of part one
Tiberius negotiates the truce at Numantia in northern Spain
Senate-backed mob kills Tiberius and hundreds of followers
Civil war between Marius and Sulla, proscriptions and mass killings
Clodius builds a political street gang; feud with Milo ends in 52 BCE
Augustus disarms the city and creates the urban cohorts and vigiles
Police force enables execution of a whole slave household under Nero
Frumentarii turned into a secret police and spy service
Praetorians auction the throne after Commodus; Severus replaces the guard, 193

notes: Transcript calls Clodius 'Claudius' (and notes the spelling change); named here as Publius Clodius Pulcher. Founding myths (753 BCE) treated as background; covered span starts at the 509 BCE revolt. Covered end set to 193 (Severus remakes the guard); the brief quote on later frumentarii and agentes in rebus is too short to extend it. No subject kind fits a polity well, so the primary is the fall of the Republic as an event.
